_readme: Labelled question -> CO corpus for the tagger evaluation harness.
Gold labels are the CO a question actually assesses, judged from the CO
statements in the same fixture -- not from what the tagger happens to say.
Where a question genuinely straddles two outcomes it is marked
difficulty 'ambiguous' and the gold label is the dominant one; those are
the questions the tagger is expected to flag rather than assert.
'hard' marks a question whose vocabulary does not overlap its outcome:
acronyms, synonyms, or a topic named in the syllabus but not in the CO.
These are the realistic failure cases and the reason the corpus exists.
Questions are written in the style of AKTU end-semester papers: a command
verb, the subject, and often a given case.
SPLIT. Each course is 'dev' or 'holdout'. Tuning is done by looking only
at dev failures; holdout is scored but never inspected while changing the
scorer. Without this the eval measures how well the tagger was fitted to
its own test set, which is worth nothing. The headline number to quote is

CO1.statement: Explain the architecture of a database management system and the relational data model.

CO2.statement: Apply entity-relationship modelling to design a normalized relational schema for a given application.

CO3.statement: Construct SQL queries to retrieve and manipulate data from a relational database.

CO4.statement: Analyze transaction schedules for serializability and recoverability.

CO5.statement: Evaluate concurrency control and recovery techniques for a given workload.

questions.text: Explain the three-schema architecture of a DBMS with a neat diagram.
Describe the relational data model and define the terms relation, tuple and attribute.
Differentiate between physical and logical data independence.
What are the responsibilities of a database administrator?
Draw an ER diagram for a library management system and convert it to a relational schema.
Apply entity-relationship modelling to design a schema for a hospital, showing cardinality of each relationship.
Normalize the given relation up to BCNF, stating the functional dependencies at each step.
Explain generalization, specialization and aggregation with suitable examples.
Write SQL queries to find the second highest salary from an employee table.
Construct SQL statements using GROUP BY and HAVING to list departments with more than ten employees.
Write nested and correlated sub-queries to retrieve employees earning more than their department average.
Explain the difference between inner join, left outer join and full outer join with an example of each.
Determine whether the given schedule S is conflict serializable using a precedence graph.
Analyze the given schedule for recoverability and cascadelessness.
State the ACID properties of a transaction and explain how atomicity is enforced.
Is every view serializable schedule also conflict serializable? Justify with an example.
Compare two-phase locking with timestamp ordering for concurrency control.
Evaluate the suitability of optimistic concurrency control for a read-heavy workload.
Explain log-based recovery with deferred and immediate database modification.
Discuss how deadlocks are handled in a database system.

CO1.statement: Explain the functions and structure of an operating system.

CO2.statement: Apply CPU scheduling algorithms to compute waiting and turnaround times for a given process set.

CO3.statement: Analyze deadlock conditions and apply avoidance and detection algorithms.

CO4.statement: Compare memory management and paging techniques in terms of fragmentation and performance.

CO5.statement: Analyze file system and disk scheduling strategies for a stated workload.

questions.text: Explain the functions and structure of an operating system.
Describe the layered structure of an operating system and state its advantages.
What is a system call? Explain the steps involved in servicing one.
Differentiate between a monolithic kernel and a microkernel.
Compute the average waiting time using SJF scheduling for the given process set.
Apply round robin scheduling with a time quantum of 4 ms and calculate turnaround time for each process.
Draw the Gantt chart for the given processes under priority scheduling and compute the average response time.
What is starvation and how does ageing address it?
Apply the banker's algorithm to determine whether the system is in a safe state.
State the four necessary conditions for deadlock and explain how each may be prevented.
Construct a resource allocation graph for the given system and determine whether a circular wait exists.
Explain the difference between deadlock avoidance and deadlock detection with recovery.
Compare paging with segmentation in terms of fragmentation.
Analyze internal and external fragmentation for first-fit and best-fit allocation on the given partition list.
Compute the number of page faults for the given reference string under LRU and FIFO replacement.
Explain the working of a translation lookaside buffer and its effect on effective access time.
Analyze SCAN and C-SCAN disk scheduling for the given request queue.
Compute the total head movement for the given request queue under SSTF disk scheduling.
Compare contiguous, linked and indexed file allocation methods.
Explain the structure of an inode and how it supports large files.

CO1.statement: Analyze the asymptotic time and space complexity of algorithms.

CO2.statement: Apply divide-and-conquer and greedy strategies to solve computational problems.

CO3.statement: Design dynamic programming solutions for optimization problems.

CO4.statement: Compare algorithm design paradigms for a given problem in terms of efficiency.

CO5.statement: Explain the classes P, NP and NP-complete and identify problems within them.

questions.text: Analyze the time complexity of the given recursive algorithm using the master theorem.
Define big-O, big-omega and theta notation and analyze the asymptotic growth of the given function.
Solve the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n log n by the substitution method.
Apply the divide-and-conquer strategy to sort the given array using merge sort.
Apply a greedy strategy to solve the fractional knapsack problem for the given items.
Construct a Huffman code for the given character frequencies and compute the average code length.
Find the minimum spanning tree of the given graph using Kruskal's method.
Design a dynamic programming solution for the 0/1 knapsack problem.
Design a dynamic programming algorithm for the longest common subsequence of two strings.
Develop a matrix chain multiplication solution for the given dimensions and state the optimal parenthesization.
Compare greedy and dynamic programming approaches for the given optimization problem.
Compare the efficiency of backtracking and branch-and-bound for the given search problem.
Which paradigm would you select to solve the single source shortest path problem, and why?
Explain the classes P, NP and NP-complete with examples.
Identify whether the vertex cover problem belongs to NP-complete and justify your answer.
Explain polynomial time reduction and show that the clique problem reduces to the independent set problem.

CO1.statement: Explain the fundamental principles of digital communication systems.

CO2.statement: Apply sampling and quantization techniques to convert analog signals to digital form.

CO3.statement: Analyze the performance of digital modulation techniques in terms of bandwidth and error probability.

CO4.statement: Design a digital communication system to satisfy specified performance requirements.

CO5.statement: Evaluate error control coding schemes for a given channel condition.

questions.text: Explain the block diagram of a digital communication system.
State the advantages of digital transmission over analog transmission.
Apply the sampling theorem to determine the Nyquist rate for the given signal.
Explain PCM and compute the quantization noise power for a uniform quantizer with 8 bits.
What is aliasing and how is it avoided in practical systems?
Analyze the bit error rate performance of BPSK over an AWGN channel.
Compare the bandwidth efficiency of QPSK and 16-QAM modulation.
Derive the probability of error for coherent FSK detection.
Design a digital communication link meeting a specified BER and bandwidth budget.
Develop a link budget for a satellite downlink operating at 12 GHz with a 3 dB margin.
Evaluate the coding gain of a convolutional code for the given channel.
Evaluate the error detecting and correcting capability of the given Hamming code.
Explain Viterbi decoding and trace the surviving path for the given received sequence.

CO1.statement: Explain the fundamental concepts and laws of thermodynamics.

CO2.statement: Apply the first law of thermodynamics to closed and open systems.

CO3.statement: Analyze thermodynamic processes using the second law and entropy principles.

CO4.statement: Evaluate the performance of power and refrigeration cycles.

questions.text: Explain the zeroth and first laws of thermodynamics with examples.
Define a thermodynamic system, boundary and surroundings, and distinguish intensive from extensive properties.
Apply the first law to a closed system undergoing a polytropic process.
Derive the steady flow energy equation and apply it to a nozzle.
Analyze an irreversible process using entropy change of the universe.
State the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements of the second law and show their equivalence.
Explain the concept of availability and compute the irreversibility for the given process.
Evaluate the thermal efficiency of the given Rankine cycle.
Evaluate the coefficient of performance of a vapour compression refrigeration cycle for the given conditions.
Compare the Otto and Diesel cycles at the same compression ratio and comment on their efficiency.

CO1.statement: Explain the structure of ecosystems and the impact of engineering activity on biodiversity.

CO2.statement: Analyze sources and effects of water and air pollution on public health and the environment.

CO3.statement: Evaluate solid waste management practices against sustainability and whole-life cost criteria.

CO4.statement: Apply environmental legislation and ethical principles to engineering practice.

questions.text: Explain the structure and function of an ecosystem with a suitable example.
Describe the causes of biodiversity loss and the concept of a hotspot.
Analyze the sources and health effects of particulate air pollution in an urban area.
Compute the BOD of the given wastewater sample and comment on its suitability for discharge.
Evaluate landfilling and incineration for municipal solid waste against whole-life cost and sustainability.
Assess the role of segregation at source in improving recovery rates.
Apply the provisions of the Environment Protection Act to the given industrial discharge scenario.
Discuss the ethical responsibility of an engineer who discovers that an employer is exceeding emission limits.
